articles.title: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.mainIdea: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.summary: Argus Research: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term. Tuesday was the third straight day when alpha came in the form of "smaller" technology stocks as well as a broad spectrum of mid- and small-cap issues. The S&P 500 tacked on another 0.6%, finishing at a minor all-time high (ATH). Meanwhile, the Nasdaq added 0.7% and the Nasdaq 100 added almost 1% -- but the two have yet to advance to an ATH. Relative strength was seen in the S&P Mid-Cap (at an ATH) and S&P Small-Cap (closing in on an ATH), which both popped 1.5%. Once again, individual stock performance was spectacular, to say the least. The leading tech stocks in the S&P 500 remain on fire, with SNDK (+27%), WDC (+17%), STX (+14%), MCHP (+12%), MU and NXPI (+10%), TXN (+8.5%), Q (+7%), and LRCX (+6%) leading the charge. The top three gainers are from the tech hardware-storage & peripherals industry, with WDC and STX exploding since April and SNDK spiking since September. Individual technology names in the S&P 400 were again huge winners, with NOVT, LITE, ALGM, CIEN, SYNA, PATH, SLAB, ENTG, AMKR, LSCC, and RRX all jumping between 6% and 12%. These are certainly not household names in tech, as the AI trade might be heading underground. The S&P Technology sector (XLK) was the third best of the 11 sectors on Tuesday, rising 1.4%. In comparison, the Equal-Weight S&P Technology sector (RSPT) led that index, bursting higher by 3%. The Small-Cap Tech sector (PSCT) tacked on 2.2%. Elsewhere, the S&P Healthcare sector (XLV +2%) came back to life, fueled by medical equipment (ISRG, SYK, MDT, A) and biotech (VRTX, ILMN, INCY, and GMAB). Both ILMN and INCY were recent technical stock selections in this report. (Mark Arbeter, CMT) Related tickers mentioned: AMZN, HWM, ^GSPC, ^IXIC, ^NDX.
